# Concurrent Male Partner Treatment for Recurrent, Symptomatic Bacterial Vaginosis

In monogamous relationships where the female partner has confirmed symptomatic,

recurrent bacterial vaginosis (defined as three or more episodes within a

12-month period), concurrent treatment of the male partner is recommended to

to reduce the risk of recurrence. Concurrent treatment should be considered

when the male partner is willing to complete a full 7-day treatment course.

Couples should agree to sexual abstinence or consistent condom use until both

partners have completed therapy. Additionally, continued condom use for at

least three months following treatment is advised to further minimize

the risk of reinfection.

# Treatment

[Metronidazole 500mg po bid x7days DI <AND> Clindamycin 2% cream apply](orz-set-abx-op-metro-500-bid-clindamycin-cream-2-male-partner)

topically to penile skin bid x 7days [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-op-metronid-500mg-bidx7days-clinda-2-cream-topical)

References:
